findings.reason: the node must be told to build the refusal from the fit check's own `estimate - window` (the context refusal `_context_fit_verdict` builds), otherwise its third done-when case can only pass on a fixture whose two estimators agree and production crashes or misreports.
findings.text: s16 says that when the chooser returns nothing the fallback "refuses with the shortfall, exit 5, whatever the competence verdict says of the resolved lane", but `routing._competence_verdict` returns `allowed: True` whenever its own estimate (standing instructions plus repository files) fits the window, and in that case it carries no shortfall at all — the reachable case, because the dispatch fit check compares the picker's `estimated_context_tokens` against the same window, so two estimators can disagree with the resolved lane measured too small by one and inside by the other — and `CompetenceLimit.__init__` (node.py:597-622) then takes its `else` branch and reads `competence_horizon_hours`/`target_size_hours`, which are absent when no horizon was measured, so the dispatch raises `KeyError` instead of exiting 5, or states a false "exceeds the competence horizon" for a lane that passed

findings.reason: the retention rule must be stated by time span covering the bound (prune only entries older than the bound plus one sweep), or the section ships a guard that fires in its own test and never on the waits it exists for.
findings.text: s6 measures stillness as "the probe's observed value has not changed for `WAIT_PRODUCER_GONE_SECONDS` (15 minutes)" from a `wait_probe_history` that `resumption.sweep` keeps as "the last few entries", but the sweep runs at `resumption.DEFAULT_SWEEP_SECONDS` of 120 s and §14 of this plan measures station ticks of 14.5 minutes, so a count-bounded history spans two to ten minutes in the ordinary case and the stillness clause can never be proven in production while a fixture that writes timestamps fifteen minutes apart passes it
